messages:
Maya: quick heads-up — after swapping the production AWQ-int8 profile to the new "hybrid-kv-shard" routing yesterday we see a slow accuracy drift on the math-fewshot suite. not a single blowup, but steady -2.5% EM over 24h.
Jason: ugh. curious if it's a scheduling/batching side-effect or quant noise. any diffs in tokenization or prompt framing?
Maya: no prompt changes. config diff is basically: awq_profile=v2, kv_shard=hybrid, batch_timeout=12ms -> used to be legacy single-shard. logging shows slightly different seq-lens distribution (more short sequences routed to shard B).
Linh: can you paste the eval run command and a sample failing case?
Maya: running here:
```bash
./run_eval.py --suite math-fewshot --model redwood-7b-awq-int8 --profile hybrid-kv-shard --seed 42 --batch 1 --out /tmp/mathev.json
```
Sample failure (expected 1, got 0):
```text
Q: If x=2 and y=3, what is x^y?
A: 8
Model: 6
```
Ryan: small numeric errors like that smell like POR (precision-of-rounding) introduced by inter-shard KV ordering — if the prefix cache is slightly different the autoregressive path can diverge.
Jason: did we repro locally by forcing shard placement to old behavior?
Maya: I ran a manual reroute: forcing kv_shard=single fixed the regression in a 5k sample run (accuracy recovered to baseline).
Linh: okay that isolates to routing. next question — is it systematic bias or random seed sensitivity? try seed sweep and mixed FP8 fallback.
Maya: did seeds 1..5, variance increased with hybrid routing: mean EM -2.4, stdev 1.1. single-shard mean EM -0.1, stdev 0.2.
ops-bot: deploy-note: rolled back hybrid-kv-shard on prod at 2026-03-20T14:12Z per @Maya request.
Jason: interesting. two hypotheses: 1) shard B uses slightly different quantized kernel ordering (different kernel pack) that changes accumulation error; 2) batching boundary changes cause different prefix cache hits — effectively adding different context in KV cache.
Ryan: we should capture intermediate logits on the same input across both configs to see where divergence starts. if logits diverge at token 1-3 it's an embedding/initial layer issue, later -> kv cache.
Maya: started a debug run that dumps per-token logits and kv-checksums for first 100 examples. command:
```bash
./debug_run.py --model redwood-7b-awq-int8 --profiles single,hybrid-kv-shard --dump-logits --dump-kv-checksum --limit 100 --out-dir /tmp/kv-dump
```
Linh: also add the quant tables and kernel versions to the dump (gptq/awq metadata).
Maya: added. initial glance: token 0 logits identical (float32 diff <1e-6). divergence begins token 2 for ~60% of failed cases. kv-checksum differs at that same token.
Jason: that points to KV routing ordering. could be non-deterministic hashmap iteration or shard assignment rounding. is there any nondet in shard placement?
Maya: placement logic uses floor(seq_len / shard_bucket) and falls back on LRU on ties — we discovered a new tie-breaker that prefers even-numbered shards to improve GPU packing.
Ryan: tie-breaker change would be deterministic but different from previous. still explains the drift. two options: revert tie-breaker or add micro-correction to quant accumulators to symmetrize.
Linh: before reverting, let's test a small patch: force identical accumulation order across shards by sorting KV keys by token index before reduce. quick patch in runtime -> run 10k eval.
Maya: patch applied, kicked off 10k run with seeds 11/12/13.
ops-bot: ci:build #7842 started (runtime-kv-sort)
Jason: if sorting fixes it, we should keep and upstream as a deterministic reduce step; cost increase should be measured.
Ryan: also run cost/latency perf: sorting adds ~0.8ms per step in our profiling — might impact latency P95. need to weigh EM benefit vs latency.
Maya: 10k results coming in: hybrid-kv-shard + kv-sort = mean EM -0.15 vs single-shard baseline, stdev 0.3. So sorting removed the regression.
Linh: nice. file a PR for deterministic reduce and add an opt-in flag to disable for ultra-low-latency workloads.
Maya: filing PR now. also adding a canary ramp for hybrid-kv-shard + kv-sort to ensure no other tasks regress (html-escape, tablex).
Jason: add targeted evals for formatting tasks — last time we saw subtle escapes break when routing changed.
Maya: noted. rollout plan: canary 1% hybrid+sort -> 5% -> 25% with monitor alerts on math-fewshot and tablex-regex.
Ryan: good. also add a synthetic microbench to measure added 0.8ms at different batch sizes (1,4,8).
Maya: will do. thanks all. :thumbsup:
